mathsRows.subject: Maths
mathsRows.originalBack: f(g(x)): apply g first, then f.
accept: The composite fg(x) is f(g(x)), so apply g before f.
fg(x) means f of g(x), with g acting first and then f.
reject: fg(x) means g(f(x)): apply f first and then g.
fg(x) means f(x) multiplied by g(x).

mathsRows.subject: Maths
mathsRows.originalFront: How do you find an inverse function?
mathsRows.originalBack: Write y=f(x), rearrange for x, then swap x and y / write f⁻¹(x).
accept: Set y=f(x), rearrange for x, then interchange x and y to give f inverse.
Rearrange y = f(x) to make x the subject, then swap the variable names.
reject: Differentiate f(x) to get the inverse function.
To find the inverse, take the reciprocal 1/f(x).

mathsRows.subject: Maths
mathsRows.originalFront: What does a one-to-one function mean?
accept: One-to-one means different inputs must have different outputs.
Each possible output has at most one input mapping to it.
reject: A one-to-one function can have two distinct inputs giving the same output.
One-to-one means every input maps to all outputs simultaneously.
